title: Nether Beast Character Study: De Jesus or Matthew (24_11)
summary: Part 2 of his Nether Beast exposé: he answers a fan's response video point by point, then lists further reasons the YouTuber was a fake natty and poor source of training advice. He refuses to let anyone dox the man's new channel.
claims: He bans anyone who links Nether Beast's new channel because he does not condone doxxing; the man has a family
Arm size means nothing unless measured; camera angles make arms look bigger
He believes Nether Beast's heavy lift clips were faked with bands hidden by camera angles; a genuine lift could be repeated on demand
Nether's pin squats used a tiny range of motion, which explains his small legs
Blowing up in size quickly and then losing about 40 lb of muscle points to drugs
Constant shoulder pain is a sign of not knowing how to train; hypertrophy training should not hurt all the time
Giving fitness knowledge for free should be the baseline on YouTube
He admits he should not have used a prohormone video as evidence because he could never find the source
Do not idolise people who teach you; novices would make gains doing push-ups and throwing rocks in the mountains
He comments on other channels for exposure without linking or asking for subscribers, which he distinguishes from spamming
Years of lifting with no results followed by sudden massive gains means either very poor training or drugs
Traps, upper back, shoulders and neck respond especially well to PEDs and shrink fast when coming off
Weight cuts do not erase muscularity; the neck shrinks over time but traps maintain fairly well
Claiming a 1000 lb raw bench is outlandish when the raw world record is around 800 lb
Nobody can be big, fast, a fighter and athletic all at once; influencers flip-flopping between bodybuilder and strength athlete are a red flag
A proper punch transfers force from the ground; leaving the ground wastes energy and leaves you unable to move
A real strength athlete shows full range of motion lifts, not partials
Anti-work rat race talk is cope; as a man you have to pull your weight
Naps were not allowed in his house growing up and he admits he is prejudiced against them
Angled Smith machine pressing is much easier than a horizontal bench; partials are fine for hypertrophy but do not demonstrate strength
